newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street stocks higher at midday, curbs lifted.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street stocks higher at midday, curbs lifted.

text.p: The Dow industrials rebounded from a morning drop and were moderately higher at midday. Trading curbs, imposed by the New York Stock Exchange amid the early decline, were lifted as of 1110 EDT/1510 GMT.

Analysts said the U.S. Consumer Price Index for May and other economic data released this morning raised no inflation fears, further strengthening Wall Street's belief that the Federal Reserve will not raise interest rates.
But the data also gave investors a chance to take profits following last week's record-breaking rally, they said.
The Dow fell more than 50 points before regaining its footing. It was up about 34 points to 7806 at midday.
The Nasdaq composite was up about eight points, or 0.55 percent, to 1440.
Dan Ascani, president and director of research at Global Market Strategists Inc, said he expects the market to continue its rally in the next couple of days.
Charlie Crane, chief market strategist at Key Asset Management, said the Dow's decline this morning was a well-deserved "breather," but he sees little to restrain the market for long.
"I think the market is going to do what it is going to do, no matter what the economic statistics are," Crane said.
May CPI rose 0.1 percent. Excluding food and energy components, "core" CPI rose 0.2 percent. The figures were in line with forecasts.
Housing starts for May fell 4.8 percent to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 1.397 million, compared to a revised April rate of 1.468 million.
U.S. industrial output rose 0.4 percent in May, compared to economists' forecast of 0.2 percent.
The 30-year bond was off 8/32 with a 6.71 percent yield. The September Standard & Poor's index futures gained 1.75 to 905.90.
Among the most active stocks, technology issues took the lead, bolstering both the Dow and the technology-heavy Nasdaq composite index.
Intel Corp surged 1-7/8 to 149-1/8 while Dell Computer Corp gained four to 119-3/8. Dell said it was very pleased with its current quarter and sees no slowing of momentum in Europe.
On the NYSE, International Business Machines Corp gained 7/8 to 90-1/4 and Digital Equipment Co climbed 1-3/8 to 38.
Equifax Inc, to be added to the S&P 500 Index after June 18, bounced 3-3/8 to 35-1/2.
Lucent Technologies Inc gained 2-3/4 to 70-1/2. It announced a consumer products joint venture with Philips Electronics NV.
NCR Corp fell 1-3/8 to 28-7/8. It said it expected second-quarter results to be below estimates due to weak services revenues and disappointing hardware systems orders.

Amgen Inc fell sharply after saying it expected sales growth to slow for its Epogen drug. It also released Phase I trial data on its obesity drug caondidate that some analysts considered disappointing. Amgen fell 2-3/8 to 59-3/4.
((--Wall Street Desk, 212-859-1730))
